findings.description: The 'data' bucket sets no ACL, no bucket policy and no public access block, and the inline comment states the bucket is public. It holds a customer master file, so anonymous principals could read (and potentially list) sensitive customer data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects containing customer data are stored without enforced server-side encryption or KMS key control.
No logging block is configured, so access to this publicly reachable bucket leaves no audit trail for detection or forensics.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy = true, so objects that are overwritten or deleted (maliciously or accidentally) cannot be recovered, weakening data integrity protection.
No bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false is attached, so objects in this public bucket can be retrieved over cleartext HTTP.

'customer-master.xlsx' is uploaded to aws_s3_bucket.data, which is public and has no default encryption, and the object itself specifies no kms_key_id or server-side encryption, directly exposing sensitive customer records.
The financials bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial records are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured for this bucket holding financial records, so access to sensitive data is not auditable.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy = true, meaning deleted or overwritten financial objects are unrecoverable.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket; the private ACL alone does not prevent a later ACL or bucket policy change from exposing financial data publicly.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so object access on this bucket is not recorded for audit or incident response.
No public access block resource guards this bucket, leaving no defence-in-depth control against a future public ACL or policy grant.
The data science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so datasets are persisted without enforced server-side encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined; the private ACL is the only control preventing a subsequent public ACL or policy grant on the data it holds.
The centralized log bucket, which receives access logs from data_science, has no public access block; log data reveals internal object names, requester identities and access patterns if exposed.
force_destroy = true with no object lock or MFA delete on the audit log bucket allows an actor with account write access to destroy the security audit trail.
